findings.title: enableSqlExpressions() contains dead and inverted logic
findings.body: `enableSqlExpressions` computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` and then returns `false` on both branches, so the computed value and the `if` are dead code and the function is a constant `false`. Two problems: (1) the polarity is inverted — `enabled` is true when the flag is *disabled* — so if anyone later re-enables the feature by deleting the trailing `return false`, SQL expressions would be permitted exactly when the toggle is off and rejected when it is on; (2) static analysis / linters commonly flag the unreachable branch and unused assignment, which can fail CI. Since this is the kill-switch for CVE-2024-9264, it should be written unambiguously (e.g. `return false` with a comment explaining that SQL expressions are disabled for security reasons), or the flag check removed entirely.

findings.title: Error text "sqlExpressions is not implemented" is misleading for an intentionally disabled feature
findings.body: When a query of type `QueryTypeSQL` arrives, the reader returns `fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")`. The feature *is* implemented in the codebase and the `sqlExpressions` feature toggle still exists and is documented as enabling it; the code path is deliberately disabled for security. Users who enable the toggle will get an error claiming the feature does not exist, with no hint that it was disabled on purpose, making the behaviour hard to diagnose and contradicting the toggle documentation. Either reword the error (e.g. "SQL expressions are currently disabled") or update/remove the toggle documentation accordingly.

findings.title: No tests guard the newly disabled SQL-expression path
findings.body: This PR disables SQL expressions (the fix for CVE-2024-9264) by stubbing `sql.DB` so every method returns "not implemented" and by short-circuiting `QueryTypeSQL` in `pkg/expr/reader.go`, but it adds no test. There is nothing that asserts that `ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery` rejects a `sql` query (including when `FlagSqlExpressions` is enabled) or that `NewSQLCommand`/`SQLCommand.Execute` fail, so a future refactor could silently re-enable the vulnerable path. Conversely, any pre-existing unit tests that exercise `sql.TablesList` or the SQL command end-to-end will now fail because `RunCommands` always errors — those need to be updated in this PR as well.

findings.title: Dead DuckDB-specific SQL string interpolation left behind in parser
findings.body: `TablesList` still builds `SELECT json_serialize_sql('%s')` by interpolating the user-supplied `rawSQL` after only replacing `'` with `''`. This is unreachable today (the stubbed `DB.RunCommands` always errors), but it is the exact pattern that made arbitrary SQL/DuckDB execution possible, and the escaping is engine-specific and incomplete (it does not handle backslash escapes or dollar-quoting). Leaving it in place means that whenever a real `DB` implementation is wired back into `NewInMemoryDB`, the injection surface is restored silently. Consider deleting the DuckDB AST parsing code along with the dependency, or at minimum parameterising the statement and adding a comment that this code is intentionally inert.
